steps.content: Manphist sucks in a ragged breath. Gone is the scholarly composure that usually defines him, replaced by the desperate exhaustion of a cornered beast and a stubborn, lingering arrogance.
Yet, behind his glasses, those clouded eyes still hold a glint—the sharp, calculating cunning of a veteran spy.
You've hit a wall. Interrogation will yield nothing more.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I understand. You did everything you could.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: He's an old fox who has lived on a knife's edge for decades. It would be strange if he did have any obvious weak spots.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What's the next step? Are you going to use more forceful methods?
With her gaze fixed on Manphist, Hilda gives you a firm shake of her head.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: That won't be necessary. Since he refuses to talk... I'll just see for myself.
She stands up and approaches Manphist.
(transition with sound of footsteps)

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Is it your turn now, Hilda? What new trick do you have for your old mentor?
Hilda stands before him, her face a landscape of sharp angles and deep shadows under the harsh white light.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I do have a new method. One that perhaps you yourself bestowed upon me.
She raises her right hand, pressing two fingers to the center of Manphist's sweat-slicked forehead, then flicks her wrist.
The air doesn't crackle, yet the world bends. Reality warps silently around her touch, and from that focal point, a torrent of living darkness erupts, coiling around Manphist's head like a serpent.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: GAAAHHHH!!!
His scream is a brief, tearing sound, too shrill to be human. But what follows is more terrifying.

A blood-curdling sight unfolds as countless semi-transparent "intelligence strips," woven from pure Mania, are violently exorcised. They tear from his eyes, his mouth, every pore, ripped out by an unseen force.
These "strips" whip into a frenzied, swirling storm around Hilda—an ominous maelstrom of glimpsed secrets.
[CG: Mania Power]
This is the true, complete form of her power.

Anchored in the heart of the storm, Hilda remains perfectly still. As her fingers graze each spinning code strip of Mania, it halts, suspended. Then it unfurls, the distorted symbols and images resolving into sharp, legible truth.
A waterfall of secrets—scenes of trades, account numbers, the ghostly echoes of secret whispers, fragments of ambition and greed—cascades into the waiting void around, holding nothing back.
[Memory Fragment]

steps.speaker: Fraser Officer
steps.content: Mr. Manphist, or perhaps I should call you "Doctor." We recognize you as a true master of your craft, one who has completed many... notable operations in the shadows of history.

steps.speaker: Fraser Officer
steps.content: Forgive my blunt assessment, but the outcome of this war is a foregone conclusion. The Metropole Alliance is like this fish—presentable on the surface, yet compromised at its core. When the conflict concludes, DisCity's guns throughout WhiteSands will show no quarter.

steps.speaker: Fraser Officer
steps.content: When a great power falls, some choose to become splendid funerary ornaments... but I take you for a pragmatist. And pragmatic men become "living assets."

steps.speaker: Fraser Officer
steps.content: This is a "scholar visiting visa" and an "investment immigration guarantee," specially approved by the Fraser Senate. With a single signature, your designation would change from "war criminal" to "protected refugee."

steps.speaker: Fraser Officer
steps.content: Your expertise in cryptography, your intelligence networks, your personal connections... they are more than sufficient to establish a premier "Strategic Intelligence Division" in Fraser. It is a future we are very keen to realize.
[Return to present]

Manphist howls, a raw sound of pure terror, as he struggles to rise. But the swirling "code strips" coil around him like icy serpents, their grip inexorable and humiliating, and slam him back into the frigid metal seat.
Through the shrieking storm and his agonized whimpers, Hilda's voice cuts cleanly, cold and absolute as a final judgment.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Money... A DisCity Bank bearer account, ending in 7749... A Fraser Union safe deposit box, designation Gamma-7...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Power... Secret meetings at exclusive salons... The title of Chief Advisor for the "Strategic Intelligence Division"...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Wine... Romanee Conti from before the Nightfall... Women... the first chair violinist from the Golden Hall... Your retirement, Manphist, is far more splendid than the "austerity" you so tearfully described.
[Continue flashback]

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: The tide of war has turned, but considerable mop-up operations are still required.

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: Please keep the Sevael Republic under close observation. The recent council bill rejection is a diversion; a strategic-level project, codenamed "Monolith," is advancing in secret. Please obstruct it if possible, or arrange for its complete termination.

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: If successfully deployed, "Monolith" will redefine the battlefield. Its survival or elimination is now a critical variable for your upcoming arrangement in Fraser.

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: We await your findings.
<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: I have initiated the placement of reliable assets within the departments. We now have direct access to all primary intelligence.
[End of Flashback]

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: You recruited under the guise of mentorship, placing assets across departments to feed you intelligence. Casey, Edward, Nolaine... all of them are pawns in your game...
You glance at Nolaine beside you. She looks as if she's taken a physical blow, her face a ghastly, bloodless white.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: So you... willingly... became the mole who hollowed out your own home. Trading critical intelligence for a comfortable post-war life. Deserting the battlefield where you belonged!
At Hilda's accusation, a low chuckle escapes Manphist's lips. Though his voice is frail, it drips with a quiet, deliberate mockery.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Don't be so rigid, Hilda. I'm retired. Your moral code doesn't apply to me anymore.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: You know the beauty of our business? Sell to two sides, and you're a traitor. But sell to everyone, and suddenly you're a professional "information broker"—and your market value soars!

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...You are utterly beyond redemption.
Hilda stares, utterly unable to process how her mentor could be so monstrous. Manphist, however, meets her horror with a deep, unbothered laugh.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: If all intelligence has a price, why should the Monolith be any different?! Besides, the truth it hides is far more corrupt than anything I've done. I may have lost my conscience, but selling that? That was genuinely liberating!

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: You have no idea, do you? Oh, of course you don't. You don't know what the metropoles plan to do with it. You're my most brilliant, yet most foolish student, handing them a knife while preaching about loyalty and justice.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: And now you have this... power. So you can read minds, can you? Then I don't need to tell you anything. See for yourself. Take a good, long look!
The next moment, he does the unthinkable. His own hands claw at the code strips constricting him, and with a violent wrench, he forcibly tears his own memories bare before your eyes.
[Continue flashback]
Manphist eyed the black-clad figure with deep unease. The operative, a special contact introduced by Fraser, had come bearing top-secret intelligence that required his deciphering skills.

Since entering, the man had pointedly kept his scarf and hat drawn low, obscuring his features. But a referral from Fraser was a powerful credential, so Manphist had accepted the stack of telegrams. Most contained standard fare—military movements, political appointments—but two stood out, their contents stark and alarming.

Recipient: Lighthouse Sender: Red Crossbill DisCity Reaper sample obtained. Shows minimal commonalities with Ash Crystal. Can proceed as a new research initiative. Response: Continue acquisition. Begin limited tests within military units.

Recipient: <color=#fb9259>Lighthouse</color>
Sender: <color=#fb9259>Mayfly</color>
<i>"Operation Raider" approval granted. Nuclear network now covers all key DisCity facilities with 160 units total, capable of a comprehensive strike.
Two days ago, "Black Manual" and "Briefcase" were compromised. 13 units were seized and decommissioned by enemy forces, and replacements were acquired.
Vulnerabilities persist. Requesting a more robust encryption system to secure the operation.<i>

Response: <color=#fb9259>Consider deploying "Monolith."</color>
As the final code was broken, the visitor gave a nod of clear satisfaction. He laid a "token of appreciation" on the table and turned to leave.
At the door, he paused, glancing back, and asked Manphist a question: Do you know what the Monolith is? Any information would be worth a fortune.
[End of Flashback]
Hilda's eyes fly open, a strangled gasp catching in her throat as if seized by an invisible hand.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: How... could this be?
Her voice is a ghost of a sound, as if her very soul recoils from the truth. Each word seems to sear her throat on its way out.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: It's impossible... This is madness... A plan like this would never pass the Joint Council!

And you understand. The revelation of 160 warheads—a network poised for nuclear strike—strikes you with the force of a physical blow. For such a plan to be approved, the metropoles wouldn't just be misguided; they would be utterly, criminally insane.

But the true devastation is the Monolith. The project she believed was her city-state's ultimate shield is, in fact, the key to this very plan. Unknowingly, she has built the very weapon that could end it all, becoming a silent accomplice to an unimaginable crime.
You can almost hear it: the sound of something fundamental within her shattering beyond repair.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Still so naive, Hilda. The Council is just another marketplace. All their grand speeches about risk and peace? In practice, it's all business!

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Isn't the Nirvana explosion proof enough?
Manphist, oblivious to the shifting atmosphere, continues his lecture. Hilda, however, purses her lips, already preparing a deliberate denial.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: That was different. Nirvana had concentrated a massive stockpile of experimental weaponry and laboratories, including the Reapers. I understood the threat... we had no other choice...

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Excellent. You've just demonstrated another classic fallacy. Intelligence operatives are often deceived by the very intelligence they handle, mistaking institutional authority for moral justification.
With a smug smirk, Manphist rips away the shell, violently exposing the metropoles' true nature.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: No matter its military value, Nirvana was fundamentally an economic port. When the bombs fell, countless civilians hadn't even begun to evacuate.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: You've been fooled, Hilda.

The way he looks at Hilda has changed. He no longer watches her as a teacher observing a student, but as a cold-eyed appraiser studying precious porcelain as it cracks, silently calculating the loss in value.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: No... You're justifying your own betrayal...
Hilda glares back at her former mentor. His betrayal wasn't born from their corrupted environment; it seeped out from the rot within him.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Justify? Why would I bother? I betrayed them because I saw the rot at the core and refused to be its next sacrifice! I defected to Fraser because they offered a better price and a higher chance of survival! But now it seems...

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: ...Even that deal is a poor investment.
Click, crack—
His backbone erupts, vertebra by vertebra, filling the room with a series of horrifyingly crisp cracks.
Chains snap, and code strips instantly crumble to dust. The body that once housed a refined scholar swells and contorts, its form bloating and dripping with black sludge.
With a deafening roar, the enormous monster suddenly lunges—not at you, but directly toward the Monolith bomb on the table.
